judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept exactly one frozen quantitative prediction for this realization if L lies in exactly one of these disjoint 3.4-percentage-point-resolution intervals: H-LEVEL-DILUTE, -46.16% <= L <= -39.36%; H-LEVEL-ASSOC, 13.84% <= L <= 20.64%; or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC, -76.16% <= L <= -69.36%. If L lies outside all three intervals, accept none.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The primary observable does not depend on a rheological regularity previously measured in the same chemistry family as S1C41. It is measured directly at 120 and 130 C in the AC1920+TK100-modified candidate, so no unmodified-family shared-shape transfer is used. This supports only a formulation-level rheological claim for the measured realization; broader transferability and molecular interpretation are not established.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified for the measured realization if L < -46.16% or L > -39.36%. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is directionally falsified beyond the stated 3.4% resolution if L <= -46.16%. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is directionally falsified beyond that resolution if L >= -39.36%. Results between -46.16% and -39.36% do not decisively separate the directional association and plasticization alternatives because of the resolution margin and realization-state uncertainty.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C41::M-REPEAT to measure between-preparation spread using at least three independently prepared realizations before treating the falsification as formulation-general.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: L, the mean of the directly measured matched-temperature viscosity-level changes at 120 and 130 C relative to the unmodified reactive-core reference: L = (Delta_120 + Delta_130) / 2, in percent. The individual Delta_120 and Delta_130 values remain reported, and E_eta is ancillary.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41::M-SWEEP is the defensible direct probe among the supplied cards: it measures the processing-temperature levels in the modified chemistry and avoids unsupported shared-shape transfer. Its main value is hypothesis discrimination rather than mitigation because it does not measure the 120 C residence-time drift failure mode. The outcome therefore supports or falsifies only formulation-level rheological prediction rules for the measured realization, not a molecular mechanism or durable hot-hold performance.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I follow the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator on selecting S1C41::M-SWEEP, but follow the Skeptic on interpretation. planner.chemistry_support_statement: The shared local temperature-response regularity was measured primarily in the original E1–E3 reactive PUR chemistry family, with E2 as the reactive-core anchor; the E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is a separate compatibility check rather than part of the primary same-composition fit. An experiment using nonzero acrylic-like or minor-tackifier-like loading would leave that directly measured chemistry support, so the shared shape cannot be assumed and a direct temperature sweep is required unless a chemistry-applicability audit establishes otherwise.
planner.failure_mode: Excessive isothermal viscosity rise during hot-melt residence at 120 °C, creating a risk of leaving the processing-viscosity window over time.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal hold increased by SI_15_60 = 0.5154 (51.5%) and SI_15_90 = 0.9308 (93.1%) at 120 °C. By comparison, E1 increased by 9.51% and 16.85% over the same respective windows. These are measured single-run trajectories, so the magnitude is established but its repeatability and formulation generality remain unresolved.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have local hold data, each represented by one four-point run at 120 °C over 15–90 min. No hold trajectory is available for E2 or for any acrylic-like or minor-tackifier-like candidate. In contrast, temperature response has six-point 80–130 °C sweeps for E1–E3 and multiple E2 runs, while realized level is measured across those sweeps despite substantial E2 run spread.
measurement_requirements: Use a nonzero modifier loading because the unmodified E2 anchor has no differential prediction and cannot distinguish the registered level hypotheses.

Measure viscosity directly from 80 to 130 °C in 10 °C increments, including direct observations at 120 and 130 °C; do not infer the processing-window level from a one-point anchor unless chemistry-shape applicability is first established.

Compare the measured matched-temperature level with the frozen inert-dilution prediction and classify it as above, within, or below measurement resolution; use at least the 3.4% direct-sweep discrimination threshold unless repeatability establishes a larger practical resolution.
Use at least three independently prepared realizations with controlled and recorded process history because E2 showed sample CV values of 0.464–0.585 and max/min ratios of 2.80–3.57 across 80–130 °C.
Run a matched-window 120 °C hold with measurements at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min on at least two independent preparations and report SI_15_60 without extrapolation.
Preserve the source viscosity unit as unknown unless the upstream audit resolves it, and keep realized level, temperature response, and isothermal drift as separate observables.
planner.scientific_question: For a nonzero modifier loading on the E2 reactive-core anchor, does the directly measured viscosity level at 120–130 °C lie above, within, or below the inert-dilution prediction after controlling preparation state, and does that formulation avoid the large 120 °C residence-time drift observed locally? The level outcome separates H-LEVEL-ASSOC from H-LEVEL-DILUTE and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is resin-modified AC1920+TK100 chemistry, outside the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family in which the shared thermal-response shape was measured. Therefore a one-point M-ANCHOR reconstruction is not scientifically supported before shape verification. M-SWEEP measures the decision-temperature levels directly and establishes the response shape in this chemistry. Its composition is inside both externally supported regions: 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier.
hypotheses_not_separated: None among the three registered level hypotheses; however, M-SWEEP does not separate any thermal-hold-drift hypothesis because no such hypothesis is included in the registered level registry.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: Using the 3.4% direct-sweep resolution, agreement with exactly one frozen S1C41 prediction would support that formulation-level hypothesis: approximately -42.76% supports H-LEVEL-DILUTE, approximately +17.24% supports H-LEVEL-ASSOC, and approximately -72.76% supports H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. Direct observations at 120 and 130 C also establish the processing-window level without assuming shape transfer.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: A level at or below the -42.76% inert-dilution prediction falsifies H-LEVEL-ASSOC; a level at or above -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-PLASTIC; departure from -42.76% by more than the applicable direct-sweep resolution falsifies H-LEVEL-DILUTE. Thus an outcome contradicting associative elevation would be retained as genuine falsification rather than attributed to the unverified shared-shape model.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result not uniquely within 3.4% of one frozen prediction would leave the three idealized level rules unresolved or indicate behavior outside them. Given the large historical E2 preparation-to-preparation spread, such ambiguity could also reflect realization-state variation. This card does not establish 120 C residence-time drift, which remains a separate unresolved observable.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level at 120 and 130 C within the 80-130 C sweep, compared with the unmodified reactive-core level; the sweep also yields the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Higher nominal VOI and the same three-pair discrimination, but its primary decision observable is reconstructed from an unverified thermal shape in AC1920+TK100 chemistry; the audit specifically recommends M-SWEEP first.
Shares the unsupported shape-transfer problem and uses a larger 22.5% total modifier burden than S1C41 without improving the deterministic discrimination vector.
Directly addresses the declared residence-time failure mode, but separates none of the three registered level hypotheses and does not return the processing-window level.
Directly addresses substantial realization-state uncertainty but does not discriminate the registered level hypotheses or by itself determine the candidate's processing-window level.

proposer.reasoning: S1C41::M-SWEEP separates all three registered hypothesis pairs using direct 120-130 C measurements at a 3.4% threshold, stays within externally supported intervention regions, and verifies rather than assumes thermal-response transfer in the new resin-modified chemistry. It is therefore scientifically preferable to the nominally top-scoring M-ANCHOR cards despite the advisory, nonbinding audit. Its limitation is explicit: it does not test the separate thermal-hold-drift coordinate and does not itself eliminate preparation-state risk.
proposer.tie_break_justification: The five score-tied cards all use M-ANCHOR and therefore infer 120-130 C viscosity through an unverified shape transfer in modified chemistry. Although the audit is advisory, that shared scientific defect outweighs their small VOI advantage. S1C41::M-SWEEP is the highest-valued direct-sweep card and avoids this unsupported inference. S1C41 also uses the smallest total modifier burden among the tied candidate compositions while remaining in the conservative 15-20% acrylic band and the repeated approximately 5% tackifier region.

robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The proposal selects S1C41::M-SWEEP rather than one of the five tied top M-ANCHOR cards. This departure is scientifically justified: every tied top card reconstructs 120-130 C viscosity using a thermal-response shape measured only in the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family, whereas S1C41 is unvalidated AC1920+TK100-modified chemistry. The advisory applicability audit marks S1C41::M-ANCHOR inadmissible_before_shape_verification and recommends M-SWEEP. The sweep directly measures the decision-temperature levels and can establish the modified chemistry's response shape.
residual_decision_risk: The catalog card specifies only one preparation; without at least three independent S1C41 preparations and matched concurrent E2 controls, preparation-state displacement may dominate the inferred relative level change.
The 3.4% direct-sweep residual is not established as the practical between-formulation discrimination resolution given historical E2 CVs of 46.4-58.5% and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57.

S1C41 changes AC1920 and TK100 simultaneously, so net formulation-level behavior cannot be attributed specifically to acrylic association, tackifier action, joint plasticization, or interaction effects.
M-SWEEP does not measure SI_15_60 and therefore does not determine whether S1C41 avoids the declared 120 C residence-time drift failure mode.
Thermal-shape transfer should not be declared verified from this sweep without predefined comparison criteria and adequate independent preparations.
The source viscosity unit remains unresolved and should not be inferred.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection does not identify a better available card than S1C41::M-SWEEP; the Skeptic explicitly recommends retaining it. It does invalidate the proposed claim that a single preparation and a 3.4% curve-fit residual provide credible three-way formulation-level discrimination. S1C41::M-SWEEP should be implemented with at least three independently prepared S1C41 realizations and concurrently prepared, process-history-matched E2 controls, with a predefined reference statistic and empirically established practical resolution. Without those controls, the direct 120 and 130 C measurements remain valid observations, but hypothesis classification must be treated as unresolved because historical E2 preparation variability exceeds the smallest prediction separation. The dual-axis formulation also prevents modifier-specific attribution, and the sweep cannot answer the separate thermal-hold-drift question.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No tested perturbation changed the deterministic tied top set. top_experiment_set_stability, measurement_plan_stability, and intervention_family_stability are all 1.0; all recommendation_flip_boundary entries are null and survive the full 0.5-1.5 scaling sweep. Thus the proposal was not top ranked under any reported re-weighting, while the five M-ANCHOR cards remained tied at the top. The base margin to the first strictly lower card is 0.002292. These weightings do not resolve the scientific applicability failure: because the audit is advisory, the score continues rewarding low-cost M-ANCHOR cards despite their unsupported shape transfer. Treating direct measurement or chemistry applicability as a hard requirement is scientifically defensible, but it is not equivalent to any reported weight perturbation.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary 120 and 130 C viscosity levels stay inside measured support because M-SWEEP observes them directly on S1C41. The proposal correctly avoids transferring the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared thermal shape into resin-modified AC1920+TK100 chemistry. The sweep can provide the direct evidence needed to assess shape transfer, but transfer should be declared verified only after predefined comparison criteria and adequate independent preparations are applied.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The instrument can produce direct 120 and 130 C values that numerically meet the stated inequalities, so the written criteria are attainable. They are not presently decisive falsification criteria because association and plasticization use the exact -42.76% boundary without an uncertainty margin, the relative-change baseline is not measured concurrently, and the one-preparation protocol does not control the much larger known preparation-state variability.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A single realization could be classified as dilution, association, or plasticization because of preparation-state displacement rather than the registered formulation-level rule, so the claimed three-way discrimination is unsupported.
objections.objection: The claim that S1C41::M-SWEEP separates all three registered level hypotheses relies on the 3.4% direct-sweep threshold, but that number is the residual of a shared-shape-plus-intercept fit, not the practical resolution of a between-formulation level comparison. Historical E2 preparations have sample CVs of 46.4-58.5% and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57, while M-SWEEP specifies only one preparation. In particular, the H-LEVEL-DILUTE versus H-LEVEL-PLASTIC predictions differ by 30 percentage points (-42.76% versus -72.76%), which is smaller than the observed preparation-state variability scale. The proposer nevertheless declares 'None' under hypotheses_not_separated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment may classify the net S1C41 level relative to the three frozen numerical predictions, but it cannot support modifier-specific attribution to acrylic association or joint plasticization by both axes.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 15.0 wt% and TK100 is 5.0 wt%, while the reactive core falls to 80.0 wt%. With no acrylic-only, TK100-only, or matched factorial control in the proposed protocol, an elevated level cannot be attributed specifically to the acrylic-like axis, and a depressed level cannot establish that both modifiers form the proposed plasticizing continuum. TK100 effects, AC1920 effects, dilution, and AC1920-by-TK100 interactions remain confounded.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The reported percentage change and its assignment to -42.76%, +17.24%, or -72.76% may primarily reflect the chosen historical E2 reference or unmatched realization state.
objections.objection: The candidate viscosities at 120 and 130 C are directly observed, which is a strength, and the fitted E_eta descriptor is only ancillary. However, the decision observable is the percentage level change 'compared with the unmodified reactive-core level.' The M-SWEEP protocol measures only one freshly prepared S1C41 sample and does not specify a concurrent E2 control, matched preparation block, reference aggregation rule, or uncertainty calculation. Because historical E2 levels vary by factors of 2.80-3.57, the relative change is not a directly measured matched-state contrast even though each absolute viscosity is direct.

objections.objection: No chemistry-domain extrapolation objection applies to the primary 120 and 130 C levels. S1C41 is outside the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI support, but the proposer correctly rejects M-ANCHOR and selects M-SWEEP, which measures those levels directly and verifies the thermal-response shape in the AC1920+TK100 chemistry. The proposal does not reuse the unmodified shared shape to reconstruct its primary observable.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A nominally falsifying result could be declared from preparation-state noise or reference-selection error rather than a reproducible contradiction of the hypothesis.
objections.objection: The numerical falsification boundaries are physically reachable, but they omit a resolution margin for H-LEVEL-ASSOC and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC: the proposal says association is falsified at or below exactly -42.76% and plasticization at or above exactly -42.76%. More importantly, the protocol's single preparation cannot justify using 3.4% as the applicable uncertainty when known preparation CV is 46.4-58.5%. Thus the protocol can generate a number satisfying the written inequalities, but it cannot establish that the departure is larger than practical experimental uncertainty.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could be misrepresented as addressing the hot-hold failure mode or proving an acrylic molecular-association mechanism, neither of which follows from the sweep.
objections.objection: No use of the unmeasured target outcome is evident. Scope is nevertheless narrower than the stated scientific question and declared failure mode: the planner asks whether S1C41 avoids large 120 C residence-time drift, but S1C41::M-SWEEP has no hold times and cannot measure SI_15_60. The proposer explicitly admits this limitation. In addition, rheological level data can support only the frozen formulation-level prediction rule; it cannot establish molecular association of AC1920, especially with TK100 simultaneously present.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain S1C41::M-SWEEP but run at least three independently prepared S1C41 realizations, as already required by the planner, and include concurrently prepared E2 controls in matched process-history blocks. Predefine the reference statistic, confidence or reproducibility interval, and use the larger empirically established practical resolution rather than automatically applying 3.4%. If modifier-specific mechanism attribution is intended, add available single-axis comparison cards for AC1920-only and TK100-only; otherwise restrict the conclusion to the net S1C41 formulation-level response. Test the declared residence-time failure mode separately with the available S1C41::M-HOLD-120 card.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The proposed one-preparation M-SWEEP uses a 3.4% curve-fit residual as its discrimination resolution despite historical E2 preparation CVs of 46.4-58.5% and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57. Without replicated S1C41 preparations and a concurrent matched E2 reference, the claimed three-way level discrimination is not experimentally credible.
